passage: I was babysitting my cousin Harish, who's almost two. His mother had put a big mirror in the hallway. Harish walked past, stopped, and stared. He had jam on his cheek. He touched the mirror first, then his own cheek, and wiped the jam off. Then he pointed at the mirror and said, "Harish!" He pointed at me. "Jeevan." Later I picked up his toy truck and he grabbed it. "Mine!" I don't know exactly what he thinks, but he seems to know who's who now.

qa.q: What was on Harish's cheek?
qa.a: He had jam on his cheek.

qa.q: What does Harish wiping his own cheek suggest he understood?
qa.a: It suggests he understood the child in the mirror was himself, since he checked his own face.

qa.q: How could Jeevan respond when Harish says "Mine!"?
qa.a: Jeevan could say, "Yes, that's your truck," and offer turns, respecting Harish's sense of ownership.

qa.q: How does Jeevan see the change in Harish?
qa.a: Jeevan sees that Harish now knows who's who, while admitting to not knowing exactly what Harish thinks.

grounding: An older cousin observes a toddler recognizing himself in a mirror and saying mine.

"Yo-yo!" he said, patting his chest.
